'''Msgr. Bryan Walsh Children's Village '''(formerly '''Boystown''') is a facility run by [[Catholic Charities USA|Catholic Charities]] in [[Cutler Bay, Florida]]. The facility was opened in 1964 and modeled on the [[Boys Town (organization)|Boys Town]] of [[Nebraska]]. In 2018, unaccompanied minor immigrants and migrant children separated from their families at the border were housed at the center.

== History ==
The Msgr. Bryan Walsh Children's Village was formerly known as Boystown and was originally part of the [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Miami|Catholic Archdiocese of Miami]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/latest-news/article213741119.html|title=Babies separated from parents are in immigrant shelters near Miami, lawmaker says|last=Vassolo|first=Martin|date=23 June 2018|work=Miami Herald|access-date=2018-07-02|last2=Flechas|first2=Joey|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/21494700/|title=Boystown to Celebrate 20th Anniversary Today|last=Fonteboa|first=Pedro|date=10 November 1984|work=The Miami News|access-date=2018-07-02|language=en|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> It was founded in November 1964 and was based on the [[Boys Town (organization)|Boys Town]] in [[Nebraska]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/21517869/|title=Boystown -- Kids Find Somebody Cares|date=8 August 1966|work=The Miami News|access-date=2018-07-03|language=en|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Boystown was originally created by the archdiocese to help house minor refugees from [[Cuba]].<ref name=":2" /> Eventually, the facility began to take in boys over 13 who needed a home.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/21494911/|title=The Men of Boystown|last=Roberts|first=Jack|date=9 November 1976|work=The Miami News|access-date=2018-07-02|language=en|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> The shelter was meant to be temporary home and the average stay was around a year or so.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/21517513/|title=Boystown: Some Call It Home|last=Fine|first=Mary Jane|date=31 January 1974|work=The Miami News|access-date=2018-07-03|language=en|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Boystown included a [[swimming pool]], animals for the children to interact with and sports facilities.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/21516174/|title='The Work Comes First, Fellows'|date=9 August 1966|work=The Miami News|access-date=2018-07-03|language=en|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Boys went to work and school in the community.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/21516364/|title=Boystown is Not a Home; But, It's Almost As Good|last=Inclan|first=Hilda|date=7 September 1968|work=Fort Lauderdale News|access-date=2018-07-03|language=en|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Dorms in the form of air-conditioned cabins housed the boys.<ref name=":3" /> Two married couples and various counselors lived on the facility.<ref name=":3" />

== About ==
The [[Catholic Charities USA|Catholic Charities]] currently runs Msgr. Bryan Walsh Children's Village which is located in Cutler Bay, Florida.<ref name=":1" /> In 2018, the center housed unaccompanied minor immigrants.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news|url=http://www.tampabay.com/the-latest-us-rep-migrant-kids-must-be-reunited-parents-ap_floridae5c3c5721c7143819c24cd594aaa91a6|title=The Latest: US Rep: Migrant kids must be reunited parents|date=2018-06-25|work=Tampa Bay Times|access-date=2018-07-03}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> In addition, children separated from their families due to the [[Trump administration family separation policy]] were housed at the Children's Village.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.richmond.com/news/national-world/government-politics/ap/babies-separated-from-immigrant-parents-are-in-miami-shelters-lawmaker/article_4eb996b9-6f79-5aaf-b78d-558b30f8c86e.html|title=Babies separated from immigrant parents are in Miami shelters, lawmaker says|last=Vassolo|first=Martin|date=23 June 2018|work=Richmond Times-Dispatch|access-date=2018-07-03|last2=Flechas|first2=Joey|language=en}}</ref> United States Representatives, [[Debbie Wasserman Schultz]] and [[Carlos Curbelo]] both toured the facility in June 2018.<ref name=":4" />
